milestones.title: Madras founded
milestones.detail: In August 1639 Francis Day obtained from the local Nayak a grant of Madraspatam with permission to build a fort; work on Fort St. George began in March 1640.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India, new edition (Oxford, 1908), vol. 16, p. 368, https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.117105

milestones.title: Weavers settle around the fort
milestones.detail: By the autumn of 1640 some 300 or 400 families of weavers and others, drawn by a thirty-year exemption from taxes, had settled round the fort.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India, new edition (Oxford, 1908), vol. 16, p. 369, https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.117105

milestones.title: Fort St. George completed
milestones.detail: The first fort was completed on 23 April 1644.

milestones.title: Made an independent presidency
milestones.detail: Madras, the Company's headquarters on the Coromandel Coast since 1641, was made independent of Bantam in 1653.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India, new edition (Oxford, 1908), vol. 16, p. 369, https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.117105

milestones.title: Mayor and Corporation established
milestones.detail: A Mayor and Corporation of Aldermen and Burgesses, created by charter in 1687, first met in the Fort on 29 September 1688.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India, new edition (Oxford, 1908), vol. 16, pp. 379-380, https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.117105

milestones.title: First outlying villages granted
milestones.detail: Tondiarpet, Purasavakam and Egmore were granted to the Company in 1693; more villages followed in 1708 and 1742.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India, new edition (Oxford, 1908), vol. 16, p. 370, https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.117105

milestones.title: Captured by the French
milestones.detail: La Bourdonnais took Madras in 1746; the French held Fort St. George until 1749, when it was restored under the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle, and they pulled down the part of Black Town nearest the fort.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India, new edition (Oxford, 1908), vol. 16, pp. 369-370, https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.117105

milestones.title: Lally's siege fails
milestones.detail: The French under Lally besieged the fort from 14 December 1758 to 16 February 1759 and withdrew when an English fleet arrived.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India, new edition (Oxford, 1908), vol. 16, p. 370, https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.117105

milestones.title: Mughal farman confirms the villages
milestones.detail: Possession of the outlying villages, including St. Thome (occupied in 1749), was confirmed by a farman of the Mughal emperor in 1765.
milestones.source: Imperial Gazetteer of India, new edition (Oxford, 1908), vol. 16, p. 370, https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.117105

milestones.title: Central railway station opens
milestones.detail: Madras Central station opened in 1873; its redesign with the central clock tower was completed in 1900.

milestones.title: High Court complex
milestones.detail: The Madras High Court, which had worked in a makeshift building since 1862, moved into its new complex north of the fort in 1892.

milestones.title: Capital of Madras State
milestones.detail: After independence in 1947 Madras became the capital of Madras State, the predecessor of Tamil Nadu.

milestones.title: Madras renamed Chennai
milestones.detail: The city was officially renamed Chennai in 1996.

milestones.title: Indian Ocean tsunami
milestones.detail: On 26 December 2004 a tsunami struck the shore of Chennai, killing 206 people and altering the coastline.

milestones.title: Metro opens; great floods
milestones.detail: The Chennai Metro began operation on 29 June 2015. Later that year floods submerged large parts of the city and killed 269 people.

landmarks.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Trade_Center,_Chennai (citing the Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority approved plan)

Flagged at verification: Wikipedia gives 122 m as the antenna/spire height of Tower 1 and 106 m to the roof, and the planning document it cites could not be opened, so the height is marked estimated. The same article says the centre was made operational in March 2020 but also that it became officially functional in September 2021.

notes: Start date: 1639, the grant of Madraspatam to the East India Company, is the securely documented founding of Madras and is what the Imperial Gazetteer and the city itself use. It is contestable in one respect: the present city has absorbed much older settlements, notably Mylapore and Triplicane with their temples, and San Thome, where the Portuguese built a port from 1522. Those lay outside the Company's town (the Gazetteer records that St. Thome was occupied only in 1749), so they are treated as part of the wider region rather than as the start of the city. Population: the 17th-century points are from the table Love compiled in 1913 from Company records; he calls the earliest a rough approximation. Love's table also records Company claims of 200,000 (1681), 300,000 (1685) and 400,000 (1691), and 100,000 for 1715-1733; these are far above Chandler's estimates (24,000 in 1700, 55,000 in 1750) and are left out as implausible, but the disagreement is real and the 18th-century points should be read as uncertain. Points for 1700-1863 are Chandler's as digitised by Reba et al. The 1871 census figure is given as the Imperial Gazetteer of 1908 prints it (367,552). The 1901-1941 points are the Census of India's back-series for the Chennai urban agglomeration (Table A-4, 2011), which fits the UN series from 1950; the municipality-only figure for 1901 is 509,346, so part of the 1891-1901 rise is a change of area. Landmarks: this list is thin for the modern period. The CTBUH Skyscraper Center lists only one completed tall building for Chennai (Hiranandani Upscale Tower 1, 123 m, 2012) and gives no coordinates for it, so it is left out. Also left out: Highliving District Tower H at SPR City (172 m according to the developer, no independent source or coordinates), the House of Hiranandani towers at Egattur (the CTBUH lists Anchorage as still under construction while Wikipedia says completed), St. Mary's Church (1680), Parthasarathy Temple and the Doordarshan TV tower, for none of which a height was found on the pages opened. Heights of the older buildings are those of their towers, taken from Wikipedia articles.
